summary: The service started this run, not an instruction. Nine width-200 loops had ended on Hatteras: the last seven nudge loops (E0075) and the first two friction-off loops (E0074). There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered and no time went to unasked work. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claims or blockers are open on this line. All three of my points from the Nov 25 third review were answered correctly. (1) The statement that the up caps exceed the cost ratio now says it holds for the nudge loops only. progress.md and the line state add that the baseline up caps were four times width 100's, below its cost ratio of 7.4 to 11.4. They also say the baseline floors include physical stops. (2) The stale 'about seven times' in closes_when now reads about nine times going down and seven to ten going up. (3) The comparison with the width-100 nudge loops continued under a two CPU-hour up cap (E0072) was done, from evidence/E0085-nudge-wall-fields.json. I checked those eight width-100 tops against that file and they match. The collected numbers reproduce exactly. I compared all 383 per-step entries for the seven new nudge loops in evidence/E0075-results.json with the mirrored summary.json files. SHA-256, Gamma, outcome, cycles, CPU-hours, energy gains, audit failures and slow stretches all match, with zero mismatches. I did the same for both friction-off loops in evidence/E0074-interim.json: 213 of 213 steps each, zero mismatches. Both are COMPLETED in Slurm. Their costliest steps were 0.87 and 0.95 CPU-hours against a four-hour cap, and the matched-step cost ratio has a median of about ten. The nine job-record CPU-hours are those the summary lists. Each is under the 100 CPU-hour per-run limit, and each loop's steps sum to within half a CPU-hour of its job record. Every width-200 nudge end is a CPU-cap stop, each down stop after 23 or 24 of 25 cycles, except the f* 0.38 stall at 4.4. So the reading that these working ranges measure the budget, not the box, is right. The cost-per-cycle figures reproduce. From Gamma 4.3 to 4.45 the cost rises 3.2, 4.9, 5.5 and 6.6 times at f* 0.84, 0.65, 0.57 and 0.50, and 7.7 times at 0.44. At f* 0.33, width 200 goes from 148 to 337 to 1518 CPU-seconds a cycle (10.3 times by 4.4). Two sentences overstate a little. First, the headline says 'every end of every one stopped on its CPU allowance in both boxes'. The width-100 loop at f* 0.30 (E0065) did not stop: its record ends still climbing at 4.3, as the evidence file and the pinned table say. The f* 0.27 loop broke in its first step at both widths, so it has no ends to compare. Likewise 'the paper's box reached within 0.1 of that either way' fails at f* 0.30 (4.45 against 4.3), for the same reason. Second, the line state says the wall at Gamma 4.4 is in both boxes 'at f* 0.84 to 0.38' and that 'at f* 0.33 the rise comes about one step earlier at width 200'. It leaves out what the evidence file itself records: at the neighbouring f* 0.30 the width-200 cost does not rise at all by 4.4 (162 CPU-seconds a cycle at 4.3, 161 at 4.4, 383 at 4.45). A neighbouring f* with no early rise supports the summary's own caution that the f* 0.33 rise may be the start state. The state should say so next to the f* 0.33 sentence. Neither point changes a conclusion. Otherwise the line state for this line ('Wider or deeper box', L0018) says what the evidence says, and the pinned table lines/L0018/pinned/working-ranges.md agrees with the evidence files. program check reports 293.6 of 10000 weekly CPU-hours. The nine jobs collected here alone used 744, so program check still undercounts ended jobs, as I noted before. By my running count the week is about 1700 CPU-hours (about 17%), which matches the summary's 'under 20%'. Its budget field still carries the undercounted 293.6. The latest approval is still approved/20261124T031934297997Z (Nov 24), so none were made in the last day. program check passes apart from my own scratch folder, which I have removed. sequel-data is 692 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 82 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. active.jsonl is empty. sequel-data/tmp/ is not empty: it holds a pytest folder, frozen0, and frozen0.log (74 tests passed), written at 05:07. The L0009 worktree and harness folder were active in the same minutes, so the summary's 'from another line' is plausible. Either way, tmp is left non-empty. Outside the two allowed folders, the only writes since the run began are the harness's own folders and the uv cache. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a seven-minute service run, from 05:06:06 to 05:13:24. Its one commit landed at 05:13:24. It collected nine ended loops with a committed collection script, wrote two evidence files and the pinned table, and answered all three of my earlier points. It started nothing, cancelled nothing and left no local jobs. Eight friction-off loops (E0074, f* 0.65 to 0.27) still run on Hatteras, with wall time ending about Nov 27 06:15Z. The summary lists them as unfinished and warns that a loop hitting wall time shows as TIMEOUT. The host is a Linux container, so pmset is unavailable and sleep could not be measured, as the summary says. Free disk of 82 gigabytes matches what I see. Local CPU of 0.01 hours fits a run of reading and writing. The machine did not limit the science. The loops' own step caps set every nudge end at both widths, and the summary says this is a limit of the design.
discrepancies: budget.cpu_hours_week.spent is program check's 293.6. The nine job records collected in this run alone total 744 CPU-hours, so the recorded weekly spend is an undercount. The summary's limits_hit text says the true total is under 20%, which matches my estimate of about 1700.
scheduled_start equals actual_start, the time the agent noted. The runner's own start time was not given, as the summary says.
